original_question: Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Is it true that the asymptotic normalized gap between f(n) and n satisfies lim_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n = √2.4?
target_in_paper: Section 1 (Erdos Problem 1), Conjecture 1.4 (Lai [35]): determine whether lim_{n->infty} (f(n)-n)/sqrt(n) = sqrt(2.4), where f(n) is the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost exactly: it uses the same extremal function f(n), the same pairwise distinct cycle-length condition, and the same asymptotic claim with constant sqrt(2.4). It also asks for the full limit, which is exactly the stronger conjecture stated in the paper, not merely one of the weaker lim inf conjectures.
missing_details: Make explicit that f(n) is the maximum over all graphs on exactly n vertices satisfying the cycle-length condition.
Spell out that the condition means every pair of cycles in the graph has different lengths.
Note that this is the paper's conjecture/open problem, not a proved theorem.
Clarify that the conjecture asserts the full limit as n tends to infinity through positive integers; it is not only a lim inf statement.
To stay fully paper-faithful, note that no extra hypothesis such as 2-connectivity or Hamiltonicity is imposed here; those are treated separately later in the section.
refined_question:
Let f(n) denote the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which every two cycles have different lengths. Determine whether
lim_{n->infty} (f(n)-n)/sqrt(n) = sqrt(2.4).
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact statement recorded in the paper as Conjecture 1.4. In Section 1, the authors first define f(n), then cite Theorem 1.2 as an upper bound and Theorem 1.3 as a lower bound of order sqrt(n), and immediately after that state Conjecture 1.4 with the exact constant sqrt(2.4). The nearby Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 are explicitly presented as weaker lim inf versions, so the draft correctly targets the stronger full-limit conjecture rather than those neighboring problems. The only real improvements needed are to make the quantifiers and the absence of extra graph-theoretic hypotheses fully explicit.
